nodes.summary: A function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice $L$ satisfies the Gilbert condition if and only if $f$ is a modular valuation and is monotone, that is, $X \le Y$ implies $f(X) \le f(Y)$.
nodes.title: Characterization of the Gilbert condition

nodes.summary: A function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice $L$, with join $\vee$ and meet $\wedge$, satisfies the Gilbert condition when $f(X \vee Z) + f(Z \vee Y) + f(X \wedge Y) \ge f(X \wedge Z) + f(Z \wedge Y) + f(X \vee Y \vee Z)$ for all $X, Y, Z \in L$.
nodes.title: Gilbert condition

nodes.summary: A function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice $L$, with join $\vee$ and meet $\wedge$, is a modular valuation when $f(X) + f(Y) = f(X \vee Y) + f(X \wedge Y)$ for all $X, Y \in L$.
nodes.title: Modular valuation

nodes.summary: A function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice $L$ is strictly positive when $f(X) > 0$ for every $X \in L$.
nodes.title: Strictly positive valuation

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ be a strictly positive function on a lattice $L$, with join $\vee$ and meet $\wedge$. Then for all $X, Y \in L$ the Jaccard distance of $X$ and $Y$ with respect to $f$ is $d_f(X, Y) = (f(X \vee Y) - f(X \wedge Y)) / f(X \vee Y)$.
nodes.title: Jaccard distance as a single quotient

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ be a strictly positive function on a lattice $L$ that satisfies the Gilbert condition, and let $d_f$ be the Jaccard distance of $f$. Then $d_f(U, W) + d_f(W, V) \ge d_f(U, V)$ for all $U, V, W \in L$.
nodes.title: Jaccard triangle inequality under the Gilbert condition

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ be a strictly positive, monotone modular valuation on a lattice $L$, and let $d_f$ be the Jaccard distance of $f$. Then $d_f(U, W) + d_f(W, V) \ge d_f(U, V)$ for all $U, V, W \in L$.
nodes.title: Triangle inequality for the generalized Jaccard distance

nodes.summary: For a function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice $L$ with join $\vee$ and meet $\wedge$, the Jaccard distance of $X, Y \in L$ is $d_f(X, Y) = 1 - f(X \wedge Y) / f(X \vee Y)$.
nodes.title: Generalized Jaccard distance
